top_ten.why: Order-6 (negation plus mu_3) quotient on j=0 curves cuts relations and LA about 3x, with a precise ratio falsifier (<2.5) and a log-consistency check. It reuses the existing IC and is a real algorithmic change. H054 and H087 are variants of it. Limited to j=0 prime-field curves and has no binary-curve effect.

Target-only left-kernel stopping at N_dep/B about 0.92 (m=3) and 0.5 (m=2) is a real cut in relation count. It can be tested by replaying stored relation streams, and the recovered t is verified directly. H049 can share the same replay.

Quotienting by Frobenius plus the 2-torsion translation iota halves unknown classes on even-order binary curves. The falsifier is sharp (class ratio >0.6, or code already quotients), and logs are brute-force checkable at n=18. First check whether 2-torsion saturation already does this.

Gray-code Artin-Schreier enumeration over Tr(s)=Tr(b/r^2) returns an identical m=2 relation set at a claimed 8-12x fewer multiplications. Set equality makes it a clean pass or fail on a real hot loop. H024 is the m=3 sibling, and H026's cache-bound caveat is the main risk.

Batch-affine versus projective addition in GF(2^131) with CLMUL is unmeasured on the binary side, which is the main target class. It is a pure speedup on the collection hot loop with an A/A arm, and H099 supplies the Itoh-Tsujii inversion arm.

Restricting the factor base to the cofactor image subgroup raises m=3 success by h (2 for Koblitz a=1, 4 for a=0). It is a mechanism change rather than accounting, with an explicit CI falsifier on yield ratio and a brute-force membership check. The matched rho in H is cheaper by sqrt(h), so the report must carry the net gap.

Peeling plus inactivation then block Wiedemann on the core predicts >=1.5x fewer modmuls than the unfiltered matrix. It is testable on saved toy matrices with a falsifier against structured GE plus Wiedemann. H060 is a related variant, and H057 provides the threshold model.

Reading kernel coordinates from the BM sequence cuts matvecs from 3N to 2N+O(1), a 33% cut with identical output. It is a deterministic check on 3000x3000 toy matrices, and the unquestioned LA phase is the weakest-covered one.

Isotropic block pairs kill the bilinear part on dim M coordinates and are predicted to lower first-fall degree by >=2 and F4 time about 5x. The falsifier is clear (dim M no larger than random, F4 ratio <1.5). This is the largest potential decomposition-phase gain, and it merges with H038/H027.

Booth/Duval canonical key at n=131 is claimed to give 1.6-3x fewer cycles than min-over-squarings, with identical orbit partition as a hard check. It addresses the key cost in the Frobenius-orbit loop. Merge H063/H092 into the same microbenchmark. Needs a PMU host.

missing_angles: Linear-algebra is thin (4 ideas, 2 of them Spot logistics H064/H093). There is nothing on Pohlig-Hellman/CRT interplay with small prime factors of the group order, lower-precision modular arithmetic, structured elimination before Lanczos, or LA for the m=2 low-weight rows.

Decomposition and factor-base hold 43 of 100 ideas, and roughly 12 of them are variants of best-of-T subspace or coset selection (H001,H004,H008,H009,H010,H013,H014,H015,H017,H042,H072,H073). A13 already measured coset selection as near-null. This is oversupplied and unlikely to produce a first improvement.

Prime-field curves (ECCp-131, Curve25519-class) are covered only by H017, H044, H054, H087 and H097. The Weil-restriction, F4, and subspace ideas are binary-specific, and no idea covers prime-field decomposition (for example Gaudry/Diem-style degree-2 and index-calculus-for-prime-field-extension).

The large-prime / double-large-prime relation cost model has no idea, although large-prime variants are claimed integrated. There is no model for how the large-prime cut interacts with orbit quotients (H062, H057 only handle the full-rank threshold).

Nearly every cheapest_test is on n=17-31 toys while targets are n=53..131. Only H090/H097/H098/H099 touch n=53+. No idea has a scaling-extrapolation test (a fit over n with a prediction interval at n=131), so toy wins cannot be turned into a distance to rho.
No idea reports the matched-rho gap or prices unpriced native work at 0/0.1/1 GAE, apart from H049, H090 and H076. Per section 5a, each should name its rho reference.

Hybrid guess strategy for Gröbner solving (how many variables to guess, with the bilinear structure) has only H019/H022/H071. Nothing covers dedicated solvers, such as SAT or XL with the Semaev structure over GF(2) and Frobenius-twisted equations, or specialised F4 linear algebra (H030 only touches the backend).

Handbook areas underused: Chapter 8-style zeta/L-function and point-count machinery beyond Weil bounds, Chapter 11.4 factorization (only H034), Chapter 13.4 sparse structured methods (used for PLE only), isogeny/endomorphism ideas outside j=0 (H087 only), and Chapters 16-17 coding/quantum (H091 aside). The Kloosterman/Walsh family (H001,H039,H048) is reused repeatedly with little diversity.
Curve-selection has six ideas, three are closed or null (H088,H089,H086), and none addresses GLV/GLS-compatible order policy or composite-order cofactor choice.

Cross-phase composition is missing: no idea tests that two accepted gains (for example the H007 iota quotient plus the H044 order-6 quotient, or the H045 stop rule plus the H059 core) compose multiplicatively on the same session.
summary: The catalogue has 100 ideas, and three things limit it. First, coverage is lopsided: decomposition (25) and factor-base (18) hold 43 of the 100, linear-algebra has 4 (2 of them Spot logistics), and descent has 7. Second, many ideas measure a distribution or predictor rather than a changed algorithm: about 12 are best-of-T subspace or coset selection (H001,H004,H008,H009,H010,H013,H014,H015,H017,H042,H072,H073). A13 already measured coset selection as near-null, and their own predictions shrink to about 1.0x at production size. Third, about 8 are closed or admitted-null re-asks (H002,H020,H078,H083,H088,H089,H100,H065). I flagged 18 relabels, 27 duplicates (several of them chains, such as H015, H044, H024/H026 and H097/H099), and 36 weak ideas. Relabel examples are H050, H090, H086, H084, H076, H062, H064/H093, H095, H077. The strongest first-improvement candidates change something countable and have a checkable output: group-structure quotients (H044, H007), early stopping (H045), identical-output hot-loop rewrites (H026, H097, H098), the cofactor factor base (H012), core extraction before Wiedemann (H059), a 33% matvec cut (H066), and isotropic F4 pairs (H041). Merge the duplicate chains before spending runs. Add LA, prime-field, large-prime accounting and scale-extrapolation ideas. Every winner must report the gap to the matched rho with the section 5a pricing band."]
